author: Dev-next-gen
body:
#### PR description:

This builds on #52335 and contains its commit; only the last commit, "Compute the helix radius from pT", belongs to this PR. Please review and merge #52335 first.

In `TwoTrackMinimumDistanceHelixLine::updateCoeffs` the helix radius was computed as `Hn * sqrt(1 - pz^2 / Hn^2)`, with `Hn` the single-precision momentum magnitude. For forward tracks this cancels: at |eta| ~ 3 the relative error on the radius is ~1e-5, and the point of closest approach of a prompt track to the beam line lands microns to tens of microns away from its production vertex. The radius is now computed directly from px and py in double precision. A separate unit test, `TwoTrackMinimumDistanceHelixLineForward_t`, checks that forward prompt tracks (pT 2-10 GeV, eta 2.4-3.0) seen from 12 cm come back to their vertex within a micron.

Why it depends on #52335: on master alone the Newton iteration is so sensitive to its input that changing the radius in the last digits flips a few borderline tracks between failure, the farthest point and the right point. On top of #52335 that no longer happens, so I only validated it there.

#### PR validation:

Same setup as #52335: CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-27-2300, el9_amd64_gcc15.

- `scram b` builds without warnings. `TwoTrackMinimumDistanceHelixLineForward_t` passes (0 failures out of 144). It fails 80 of them both on master and with #52335 alone.
- Standalone check against a brute-force reference, 100k tracks per sample, comparing #52335 alone with #52335 plus this PR. Prompt tracks with an error above 10 m: 77  0. Tracks displaced up to 60 cm: 687  11; there are also 11 tracks off by more than 1 mm with #52335 alone, which this PR does not change in number. No new failures in any sample. Individual points move by 0.04 m (median) and at most 20 m for prompt tracks.
- Workflows 27234.711 and 11634.0, 20 events, step3 with #52335 and with #52335 plus this PR. No failures in either, and no track moves by more than 1 mm. Almost every track moves slightly, as expected since the radius changes for all of them: the vertex position moves by 0.01-0.7 m (median, depending on the collection) and at most 74 m. `generalTracks` in 11634.0: 3046  3047.

This one changes every track by a small amount, so I would expect it to need the usual physics validation on your side more than #52335 does.
